discrepancy_checks.diagnosis: Conical oscillation - re-teach the release step.
Period bias warning - release angle too large.

discrepancy_checks.detects: Systematic offset in the recovered constant
discrepancy_checks.diagnosis: Length measured to the wrong reference point on the bob.
Oscillation miscount in one timing row.

bom_tiers.description: Plywood/MDF + aluminium-extrusion offcuts frame, SG90/MG996R-class servo release, Arduino-class controller or direct PC control, phone/webcam timing, printed scale.
2020/2040 aluminium extrusion gantry, stepper length-adjust with lead screw, optical fork sensor timing, dedicated microcontroller, enclosed E-stop panel.
Anodised extrusion + steel pivot hardware, encoded motor, redundant timing sensors, safety relay for the monitored stop, calibration certificate workflow in-app.

machine_design_hint.description: Gantry carriage sets thread length (motorised spool/clamp, 50-100 cm), releases the bob at a set small angle with no push (electromagnet or servo gate), and times crossings with an optical gate at the equilibrium position. The lesson states honestly that the machine's optical timing method differs from the candidate's stopwatch method.

graph_spec.form: linear, line of best fit through the origin region
graph_spec.notes: Axes labelled with quantity/unit; scale fills at least half the grid; slope from a large triangle. Template also supports the T vs sqrt(L) and log T vs log L graph forms set in other years; this demo uses T^2 against L.

observation_spec.precision_notes: Ruled table; column heads as quantity/unit; consistent decimal places as per column precision.

hazards: falling stand if base is unstable
hazard_profile.notes: Mechanics practical: no heat, electricity or chemicals. Base interlock set only.

practical.outcome_spec: Recovered value of g within +/-5% of 9.81 m/s^2 (target +/-3%), computed identically from the teacher's readings, the simulation, and the machine's runs.
practical.subject: Physics

practical.title: Simple pendulum: determination of g from period and length

precautions: The bob was displaced through a small angle and released without a push, and conical oscillation was avoided (oscillation kept in one vertical plane).
Timing was started and stopped as the bob crossed the fiducial mark at the equilibrium position, and the apparatus was shielded from draught / the support was firm.

steps.check_question: From where to where is L measured?
steps.expected_observation: Apparatus rigid; length reference point identified.
steps.narration: Set up the stand, clamp, split cork, thread and bob. Check the zero error. Measure L from the pivot to the centre of the bob.
safety_notes: Confirm the stand base is stable before suspending any mass.
steps.title: Set up the apparatus

steps.check_question: Why is L recorded to one decimal place?
steps.narration: Adjust the thread at the split cork until L is 90.0 cm.
steps.title: Set L = 90.0 cm

steps.check_question: What goes wrong if the bob is pushed or released at an angle to the plane?
steps.narration: Displace the bob through a small angle, about ten degrees, and release it without pushing, so it swings in one plane.
steps.title: Displace and release without a push

steps.expected_observation: Two close timings t1 and t2 for 20 oscillations.
steps.narration: Start and stop the watch as the bob crosses the fiducial mark at the equilibrium position. Time twenty complete oscillations, twice, and take the mean.
steps.title: Time 20 oscillations, twice

steps.check_question: What pattern do you expect in t as L decreases?
steps.expected_observation: A complete set of timings, one row per length.
steps.narration: Shorten the thread and repeat the timing for L = 80, 70, 60 and 50 cm.
steps.title: Repeat for L = 80, 70, 60, 50 cm

steps.check_question: Why do we square T before plotting?
steps.expected_observation: A ruled table with quantity/unit column heads and consistent decimal places.
steps.narration: Tabulate L, t and the mean t. Evaluate T = t/20 and T squared for each length.
steps.title: Tabulate and evaluate T and T^2

steps.check_question: Why must the slope triangle be large?
steps.expected_observation: A straight line through the origin region; slope about 4.03 s^2/m.
steps.narration: Plot T squared against L. Draw the line of best fit and find the slope from a large triangle.
steps.title: Plot T^2 against L and find the slope

steps.check_question: What would a systematically wrong length measurement do to your value of g?
steps.expected_observation: g approx. 9.8 m/s^2, within the tolerance band.
steps.narration: Evaluate g = 4 pi squared divided by the slope, and compare with the accepted value.
steps.title: Evaluate g and compare

steps.check_question: Why is 'I avoided errors' not a creditworthy precaution?
steps.narration: State two precautions you took, in the past tense, naming the error you avoided and the action you took.
steps.title: State two precautions
